summary: Connection factory package. create_connection(profile, auth_profile) validates the auth mode against the profile spec's supported_auth, maps the provider to a leaf connection class and an auth-client TargetFamily, and builds connect kwargs by layering auth_profile.emit() over profile.emit() (with a boto Session/assume-role envelope for S3 ROLE_ARN/PROFILE_NAME). create_tunnelled_connection builds an SSH-bastion TunnelledConnection. The package also defines the TransportConnectionError hierarchy, NullConnection for local storage, the OAuth2 refreshable-auth adapter, and re-exports auth-client OAuth flow helpers for backward compatibility; importing it requires the [http] extra.
public_api: OAuthFlow, OAuth1Flow, LocalCallbackServer, extract_code_from_input, prompt_for_code (legacy re-exports from mountainash_auth_client)
key_classes: TransportConnectionError — base exception for connection operations (not a StorageError)
UnsupportedAuthProfileError — auth mode outside spec.supported_auth, or an OAuth authorization request transport does not handle
TokenExchangeError / TokenRefreshError / AuthorizationRequired — legacy OAuth error types kept for compatibility
NullConnection — always-connected no-op connection with client None, used for local storage
OAuth2RefreshableAuthStrategy — thread-safe RefreshableAuthStrategy over auth-client's OAuth2TokenManager (get_headers acquires, refresh forces refresh)
key_functions: create_connection(profile, auth_profile=None, *, auto_authorize=False) -> ConnectionProtocol — validate auth, emit kwargs, return an unconnected leaf/decorator connection

create_tunnelled_connection(bastion_profile, bastion_auth, target_profile, target_auth, remote_host, remote_port) -> TunnelledConnection — SSH bastion chain whose inner connection targets 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral port>

create_auth_strategy(auth_profile, *, oauth_provider=None, token_store=None) -> OAuth2RefreshableAuthStrategy | None — managed OAuth2 strategy or None for static tokens; fails closed on misconfiguration
_emit_kwargs(profile, auth_profile, family) -> dict — kwargs assembly incl. boto Session envelope; rejects ROLE_ARN for r2/minio/b2
extension_points: _PROVIDER_CONNECTION_MAP and _PROVIDER_FAMILY_MAP (private dicts) map provider strings to leaf classes and TargetFamily; adding a provider means editing these maps
Any object implementing ConnectionProtocol can be supplied as a tunnel inner connection via create_tunnelled_connection's inner factory
Profiles may implement emit(family) to control kwargs; otherwise to_handler_kwargs() is used
Profile __spec__.supported_auth drives auth-mode enforcement; specless profiles skip it
lifecycle_notes: create_connection returns an unconnected connection and performs no I/O; the caller (normally StorageFacade) calls connect().
Package import raises MissingExtraError naming [http] when mountainash_auth_client is absent; leaf SDKs (boto3, paramiko) are imported lazily in connect().
SFTP profiles produce SFTPConnection(SSHConnection(...)); decorators exclusively own their inner connection.
auth-client owns token acquisition/refresh; transport only adapts OAuth2TokenManager to the HTTP engine seam. Token stores are caller-owned.
auto_authorize is accepted but unused in the current implementation.
documentation_hooks: Connections overview: leaf vs decorator connections and the create_connection pipeline
Profile + auth separation: how storage profile emit and auth profile emit combine per TargetFamily
S3 assume-role / named AWS profile envelope and flavor restrictions
Managed OAuth2 via create_auth_strategy and token stores
Connection error hierarchy and its relation to StorageError
examples: examples/auth_compatibility/example.py — create_connection rejects an incompatible auth profile with UnsupportedAuthProfileError before any I/O
risks: Unknown or None provider types silently fall back to HTTPConnection (_connection_for_provider), so a misdeclared profile builds an HTTP client instead of failing.

connections.errors defines ConnectionError as an alias of TransportConnectionError, shadowing the builtin ConnectionError for star-importers; TransportConnectionError is not part of the StorageError hierarchy.
auto_authorize parameter is accepted but ignored, which can mislead callers expecting an interactive flow.

Legacy OAuth re-exports (OAuthFlow, LocalCallbackServer, etc.) tie the package surface to auth-client internal module paths; the module docstring still describes 'OAuth flows, callback servers' as transport infrastructure.
create_connection returns ConnectionProtocol[Any]; the client type is runtime-dependent (docs/typing.md dynamic boundaries).
open_questions: Should the legacy OAuth re-exports and ConnectionError alias be deprecated on a schedule?
Should unknown provider types raise instead of defaulting to HTTPConnection?
Is auto_authorize intended to be removed or wired up?
Boundary: this module bundles factory, errors, NullConnection and the OAuth2 adapter; should auth_strategy.py be profiled separately as an HTTP-auth integration?

evidence.detail: Root exports create_connection, create_tunnelled_connection, SSHConnection, SFTPConnection, TunnelledConnection, TransportConnectionError
create_connection enforces supported_auth then selects leaf via _PROVIDER_CONNECTION_MAP with HTTPConnection default; legacy OAuth re-exports
Facade calls create_connection, create_auth_strategy, then connection.connect()
Public use of create_connection and UnsupportedAuthProfileError
Importing mountainash_transport.connections on base install raises MissingExtraError('http')
Frequent changes June–Oct 2026 (auth enforcement, assume-role envelope, OAuth2 strategy, MissingExtraError) => evolving
